coverage: Paid pattern-first interview course (freemium). Public parts: pattern-intro lessons (binary search, heap, backtracking, topological sort, DP intro) with step-through slides, templates in up to 10 languages and an in-browser test runner; free cheatsheets mapping problem keywords to algorithms and input size to complexity; a pattern-priority page; LeetCode editorials (liteproblems/<n>) that walk an algorithm-selection flowchart to the pattern. Locked (Go Pro): most family maps, decision rules, knapsack and interval lessons, the interactive flowchart and probably templates. Also an LLD/OOD course whose intro and parking-lot case study opened without a paywall (other lessons not checked); system design is outsourced to systemdesignschool.io. Many pages did not render content through fetch.

refs.title: Algorithm selection flowchart
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: Pro-listed interactive decision tree that leads from yes/no questions about the input to a pattern. Canvas did not render via fetch; editorials replay its steps (graph? sorted? linked list? then heap).

refs.title: Keyword to algorithm cheatsheet
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: Table of problem-statement cues (top k, how many ways, substring, prefix, shortest path, permutations) each mapped to a likely technique with a one-line reason. Free and compact.

refs.title: Input size to complexity cheatsheet
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: Works backwards from constraint size: for each complexity class it gives the rough max n that fits a time limit and the algorithms that usually produce it, plus a note on amortised cost.

refs.title: Which patterns to study first
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: Ranks patterns by return on study time from the site's interview data: DFS/BFS/two pointers first, heaps underrated, DP and greedy lower priority, tries and union-find last.

refs.title: Pattern code templates
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: Index of about 20 reusable skeletons (window fixed/longest/shortest, two-pointer directions, tree/graph/grid BFS-DFS, mono stack, prefix sum, union-find, trie). Access not checked.

refs.title: Binary search intro
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: Slide-by-slide walkthrough of halving the search space, safe midpoint and loop bounds, with a runnable test box and an 'explain it in your own words' prompt. Leads into a 'first true' boundary family.

refs.title: Two pointers decision rule
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: Locked lesson that, per the outline, chooses between same-direction, opposite-direction, window and fast/slow variants. Only the title and outline are public. Quality unverified (locked).

refs.title: Sliding window family map
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: Locked overview grouping window problems into fixed, longest and shortest families; the public outline is a good taxonomy even without the body. Quality unverified (locked).

refs.title: Heap / priority queue intro
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: Triage analogy for priority queues, diagrams of sift-up/sift-down on the array layout, built-in heap APIs in several languages, and a first practice problem.

refs.title: Backtracking template
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: Frames backtracking as DFS over a state-space tree you draw first, then gives one template with choose/undo and the cost analysis. Pruning and extra state come in later lessons.

refs.title: Topological sort intro (Kahn's algorithm)
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: In-degree based ordering explained with a 10-step slide sequence, related to BFS, with cycle detection and code in four languages.

refs.title: Dynamic programming intro
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: Fibonacci used to contrast memoised top-down with bottom-up tables; recipe for state, base case, recurrence; ends with a catalogue of DP shapes (grid, knapsack, interval, two-sequence) and their cues.

refs.title: Knapsack DP intro
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: Locked. Outline splits knapsack into weight-only, 0/1, unbounded and bounded sections with Partition Equal Subset Sum, Target Sum and Coin Change as practice. Quality unverified (locked).

refs.title: Intervals pattern intro
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: Locked. Outline covers merge, insert, meeting rooms I/II, non-overlapping intervals, balloon arrows and partition labels. Quality unverified (locked).

refs.title: Merge k Sorted Lists editorial
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: Editorial that first walks the selection flowchart step by step to justify a heap, then intuition, example trace, pitfalls and complexity; includes a stepping state visualiser.

refs.title: Low-level design course
refs.subject: ood
refs.summary: Full LLD track: 6-step delivery method, OOP and UML with an exercise per lesson, SOLID plus DRY/KISS/YAGNI, 14 GoF patterns, a concurrency module, then 15 case studies. Paid status per lesson not shown.

refs.title: LLD design patterns overview
refs.subject: ood
refs.summary: Entry to the patterns module (factory, builder, singleton, adapter, decorator, facade, proxy, strategy, observer, state, command and others), each followed by an exercise. Seen in outline only. Access not checked.
